title: When will I get married? What Vedic astrology can actually say | Ask Tota
description: Marriage timing in Vedic astrology comes from the 7th house, its lord, Venus, and the dasha running. Here is the real method, the windows it gives, and why exact dates are a sales pitch.
og_title: When will I get married, honestly answered
og_description: The 7th lord, Venus, the dasha and the Jupiter transit. Here is how marriage timing is actually calculated, and why nobody can hand you a date.
h1: when will i get married, and what a chart can actually say
dek: vedic astrology times marriage from the 7th house, its lord, venus, and whichever dasha is running. what that produces is a window of a year or two, not a date. here is the whole method, and the honest limits on it.

faq.q: can vedic astrology tell me exactly when i will get married?
faq.a: no. the method produces windows, usually a year or two wide, from dasha periods and slow transits. anyone naming a month and a year is going past what the technique can support.

faq.q: which house shows marriage in a birth chart?
faq.a: the 7th house and its lord carry partnership. the 2nd house of family and the 11th house of fulfilled desires get read alongside it, and the 8th is used for the durability of the bond.

venus is the karaka for partnership in every chart, regardless of gender. jupiter is weighted heavily for marriage in a woman's chart in the classical texts, which is a convention of those texts and worth naming as one.

the periods most often cited are those of the 7th lord, any graha sitting in the 7th, venus, and the lords of the 2nd and 11th. a mahadasha and antardasha that both point at partnership is the strongest signal the system has.

faq.q: does the jupiter transit affect marriage timing?
faq.a: it is the most used transit for it. jupiter takes about twelve years to go round, spending roughly a year per sign, and its passage over the 7th house, the 7th lord or the natal moon is a classic timing trigger.

faq.q: what is the double transit rule?
faq.a: a gochar principle where a house is considered activated when both jupiter and saturn influence it at the same time, by placement or aspect. for marriage it is applied to the 7th house from the lagna and from the moon.

faq.q: does the navamsa chart show marriage timing?
faq.a: it shows the register of partnership, not the timing. timing lives in the dasha sequence and the transits. the navamsa is used to check the quality and strength of what the 7th house is promising.

faq.q: why do astrologers get marriage predictions wrong?
faq.a: three usual reasons. the birth time is off, so the houses are off. the window given was years wide and got repeated as a date. or the prediction landed in the age band where most marriages happen anyway, so it was never really a prediction.

faq.q: what does delayed marriage look like in a chart?
faq.a: saturn's involvement with the 7th house or its lord is the most cited signal, along with a difficult 7th lord placement. delay in the classical sense means later than the social norm of the time the text was written, which is worth remembering.

faq.q: can a chart predict who i will marry?
faq.a: it can describe the register of partnership u are wired for. it cannot produce a name, a face, a profession or an initial. any reading that does that has left the tradition.

faq.q: is manglik dosha a real obstacle to marriage?
faq.a: manglik is mars in the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 7th, 8th or 12th house. it is a house position with a long list of traditional cancellations, not a verdict on ur marriage. we took it apart separately.

faq.q: does kundli matching predict when marriage happens?
faq.a: no. ashtakoota scores compatibility between two people out of 36 using their moons and nakshatras. it says nothing about timing, and it is a separate question from when.

faq.q: what should i actually do with a marriage window?
faq.a: treat it as a note about which years the chart is louder in, and go on living. a window that arrives while u are nowhere near anyone is just a window. astrology does not do the introductions.
